# h3_disk (Resource)

Manages a network block disk.

`size` grows in place (online, also while attached); shrinking is refused at plan time. `performance_class` changes in place. `name`, `project_id` and `storage_class` force a new, empty disk — protect disks with data with `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "h3_disk" "data" {
  project_id        = var.project_id
  name              = "pg-data"
  size              = "100Gi" # grows in place; shrinking is refused at plan time
  storage_class     = "replicated"
  performance_class = "R_FAST" # changes in place

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Disk name. Changing it replaces the disk.
- `size` (String) Disk size, Kubernetes quantity (e.g. `10Gi`). Increased in place without detaching; a smaller value is rejected at plan time.
- `storage_class` (String) Storage family: `replicated` (network, survives a node failure) or `local` (node NVMe). Changing it replaces the disk.

### Optional

- `performance_class` (String) Performance (QoS) class within the storage family, e.g. `R_BASIC`, `R_STANDARD`, `R_FAST`, `R_ULTRA` for `replicated` and `L_STANDARD`, `L_FAST` for `local`; IOPS and bandwidth limits grow with the disk size. The family default when omitted. Changed in place (no data movement). Available where disk QoS is enabled.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (UUID). Defaults to the provider `project_id` (`H3_PROJECT_ID`). Changing it replaces the disk.

### Read-Only

- `attached_to_vm_id` (String) ID of the VM the disk is attached to; null when detached
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp
- `id` (String) Disk ID
- `status` (String) Disk status (`AVAILABLE`, `ATTACHED`, `RESIZING`, ...)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by ID
terraform import h3_disk.example <id>
```
